title: Power Automate: generate documents from SharePoint document generation forms
summary: Hold: the governance path stops before connector classification, and the PowerShell command creates a policy without setting the connector restriction it claims to configure. The Dataverse role qualification is too broad, and the statement that Microsoft publishes no storage cost overlooks published SharePoint storage pricing.

claims.claim: Data policies govern which connectors flows in the scoped environments can combine with the SharePoint connector.
claims.quote: By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.

claims.claim: Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy reaches the control that sets which connectors a flow may combine with SharePoint.
claims.quote: Select the Data policy section. Select + New Policy. In the Pre-built connectors page, review the various attributes and settings you can make on the Assign connectors screen. Select the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors, and then select Move to Business from the top menu bar.
claims.fix: The printed labels are present, as the pre-check found, but the path ends at the policy list rather than connector classification. Replace the path with 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > + New Policy > Pre-built connectors > SharePoint > Move to Business'. The cited page documents this route for putting SharePoint in the Business group; its later environment scope and confirmation steps remain in the reference.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -DisplayName <policy name> -EnvironmentType <environment type> sets which connectors may be combined with SharePoint.
claims.quote: The New-DlpPolicy cmdlet creates a new DLP policy for the logged in admin's tenant. -DisplayName: Creates the policy with the input display name. -EnvironmentType: The type of the environment: trial, production, sandbox, default.
claims.fix: The command and its printed parameters exist, but this invocation only creates the policy and supplies no connector classification. Replace controls[0].api.call with 'Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification Confidential -Connectors <connector objects>' and its docs URL with 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powerapps.administration.powershell/add-connectorstopolicy'. Add that URL to sources. The reference says this operation adds or moves the supplied connectors to the Business group; each connector object requires id, type and name.

claims.claim: The data policy page says SharePoint cannot be placed in the Blocked group through the Block action.
claims.quote: For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.claim: The data policy page requires Environment Admin or Power Platform admin permissions to create, edit or delete policies.
claims.quote: To create, edit, or delete data policies, you must have either Environment Admin or Power Platform admin permissions.

claims.claim: For environments with a Dataverse database, System Administrator replaces the preceding Environment Admin or Power Platform admin role requirement.
claims.quote: Tenant-level policies: sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role. Environment-level policies: you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions. For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.
claims.fix: Replace the role sentence with 'Tenant-level data policies require the Power Platform Administrator role. Environment-level data policies require Power Apps Environment Admin permissions, or the System Administrator role for environments with a Dataverse database.' The Dataverse exception replaces Environment Admin for environment-level policies, not Power Platform Administrator for tenant-level policies.

claims.where: Governance controls: tenant switch; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not document a tenant-wide switch specifically for document generation forms or their three Power Automate operations as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "document generation forms" "tenant" disable admin; "document generation" "Set-SPOTenant" disable forms. Read structured document generation, connector guidance and reference, and returned Set-SPOTenant excerpts; no feature-specific tenant switch found.

claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to check library permissions and assigned Copilot licences, but the controls table contains only a data policy row.
claims.quote: Review Edit permissions on the libraries; Check which Microsoft Copilot licences are assigned; Review the destination libraries for who can open the generated documents. The sole controls row governs which connectors flows may combine with SharePoint.
claims.fix: The Before rollout checks of library Edit permissions and assigned Copilot licences, and the After rollout check of document access permissions, have no corresponding controls-table rows. The tenant-switch absence stated in Governance controls is also not represented in the table.
